correctness.rationale: All m,n>=2. An unselected neighborhood for some cell (i,j) is exactly containment of S in the corresponding row-column cross. Partition failures by (r,s), the numbers of active rows and columns: empty; a single active row/column; (2,2) with 2 diagonals and 4 triples per rectangle; (2,s>=3) and (r>=3,2) with a unique singleton row/column; and (r,s>=3) with unique row and column centers of a paired-star configuration and an optional central edge. Summing gives the stated B polynomial without overcounting. The 2-row factorization and minimum coefficients use the same cross criterion. An independent open-neighborhood implementation exhaustively checked 1,173,328 subsets in eleven graphs and the cross criterion on three, plus 625 exact-arithmetic parameter pairs. Finite tests are not mistaken for the proof.

originality.rationale: Originality is judged for the complete all-cardinality polynomial and its exact failing-set classification, not for scalar total-domination numbers, the definition of a total-domination polynomial, or the trivial cross witness. Defant-Iyer (2017) and Vemuri (2019) study direct products of complete graphs but give scalar domination/total-domination results rather than a full polynomial. Hu et al (2016) give general total-domination-polynomial reductions, not the present evaluated family. Mertens (2024) enumerates *ordinary* dominating sets of the *Cartesian* rook graph, whose adjacency is complementary to the graph here. Relevant search results did not imply the full stated formula. Publication priority remains provisional given unindexed literature and a partially inaccessible older paper.

value.rationale: The complete two-parameter total-domination cardinality spectrum is a natural robustness invariant for open-neighborhood monitoring in dense graph products. The disjoint row-column-support/paired-star classification enumerates every failure size and all maximal failures, identifies the exact random-probe reliability at every common activation probability, and includes exact thin-factor and minimum-set limits. The full enumerator is not implied by previously established scalar extrema and is not an arbitrary tiny parameter slice. The result is self-contained without speculative downstream claims.
